category_title: Low-achieving EFL learners exhibiting hesitation, distraction, and lack of participation in mainstream classes
scenario_title: Task avoidance and distraction in mainstream class
minimal_context: The student is working in a pair with a peer to complete an English exercise in a regular mainstream classroom.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please work with your partner to complete the exercise on the worksheet. You need to take turns answering the questions.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks at her partner's paper instead of her own) Um... okay.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What do you think the answer to the first question is?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Answers with hesitation and poor pronunciation) I... I think it is... I am not sure. She can answer it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to do your own work and participate in the pair activity.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Pulls out her mobile phone and looks down, remaining subdued) I will just let her do it. I don't want to answer.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Please work with your partner to complete the exercise on the worksheet. You need to take turns answering the questions.

STUDENT: (Looks at her partner's paper instead of her own) Um... okay.

TUTOR: What do you think the answer to the first question is?

STUDENT: (Answers with hesitation and poor pronunciation) I... I think it is... I am not sure. She can answer it.

TUTOR: You need to do your own work and participate in the pair activity.

STUDENT: (Pulls out her mobile phone and looks down, remaining subdued) I will just let her do it. I don't want to answer.

task.content: Taking turns in answering exercises and participating in groups or pairs

context.social_setting: Alongside other students who are more able than they are

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When expected to participate in classroom activities or do their own work
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Distracted (e.g. on the mobile), looked at their peers' work instead of doing their own, didn't participate in groups, and let the other person dominate when working in pairs
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Intimidated both by their lack of self-efficacy and by the fact that other students are more able than they are; do not feel safe

behavior_patterns.condition: When answering exercises voluntarily or by teacher selection
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Answers with hesitation and poor pronunciation, seems unsure of herself and isn't confident
